problems.title: Allow callers to detect an unnamed multipart form field
problems.summary: The default parser can return a partial form after dropping an unnamed field. Upstream closed issue #1569 by documenting this behavior. This fork chooses strict parsing.

commits.title: Integrate strict form parsing with HTTP 2.16 and its multipart/mixed handling

fix.why_together: The first-parent change of this merge (git cherry-pick -m 1) is the complete fix against the recorded upstream base. It reconciles the parser documentation, release metadata and regression tests with the newer upstream code. The original topic commit applies to 2.15.2.

draft.title: Allow callers to detect an unnamed multipart form field
draft.body:
HTTP 2.16 on Julia 1.10.12 documents that an unnamed field in a multipart form is skipped (#1569, #1571). An application that needs to validate the complete form cannot distinguish a missing field from one the parser discarded.

**Example.** In memory, pass a form containing two text parts to `HTTP.parse_multipart_form`. Give one part the field name `message` and omit the name parameter from the other. The result contains only `message`. A strict caller expects the parser to report the incomplete form. An explicitly empty field name is a separate case.

**Fork behavior.** The form-data parser reports a missing disposition or name. An explicitly empty name is accepted, and ordinary headerless multipart/mixed data still parses. An opt-in strict mode could provide that signal to upstream callers while preserving the documented default.
